title: King Sivi's eyes
hook: a king gives his eyes to a blind beggar (Jataka 499)

segments.voice: Yesterday: two chariots on a narrow road, and the one who wouldn't give way was the one who fell. Your line: yielding wins. Today, a king who gives up far more than the road.

Some gifts cost nothing. Spare change, an old coat, a favor that fits the afternoon. King Sivi, in the Jataka, had given plenty of those: food, clothes, money, the story says, and he still wanted to give more. One day he made a quiet wish: if anyone ever asked for a part of his own body, he would give it. Then someone asked. A blind old man came before the king and asked for an eye.
screen: `GIFTS THAT COST NOTHING.` → `A KING'S QUIET WISH.` → `A BLIND MAN ASKS FOR AN EYE.`

segments.voice: First, the test. The blind man wasn't what he seemed. The Jataka says he was Sakka, king of the gods, in disguise, come to see whether Sivi meant his wish. Second, the cost. The king's ministers pleaded: give gold, give jewels, give anything, but not your eyes. Sivi sent for his surgeon anyway. The story doesn't hurry here. It dwells on the pain, and has the king say he gives not for gain but for the sake of awakening. Once the first eye was given, he gave the second. Third, the aftermath. Blind now, Sivi left the palace and sat alone by a pond. Sakka came back and asked him to speak the truth about his gift. The king said, truthfully, that he had given gladly. On those true words, the story says, his sight returned. Fourth, how to hold a story this extreme. It isn't a recipe for harming yourself. Tradition tells it as a picture of the perfection of giving, dana, stretched as far as it can go. Its question for an ordinary Tuesday is smaller and sharper: is there a gift that would actually cost you something? An hour you'd guarded. Credit you'd love to keep. An apology that bruises your pride. Sivi's tale isn't about the size of a gift. It's about giving past the part of you that would rather hold back.
screen: `A BEGGAR WHO WASN'T A BEGGAR.` · `GIVE GOLD, NOT YOUR EYES.` · `TRUE WORDS, AND SIGHT RETURNS.` · `A GIFT THAT COSTS YOU.` · then, large: `WHAT HE GAVE.`

segments.voice: Ask yourself quietly what you could give that you'd rather keep: time, attention, a word of credit, patience with someone who wears yours thin. Don't pick the biggest answer; pick the one that's real. Then rest a while and simply notice the part of you that wants to hold on, without arguing with it.
Dana. Giving: the perfection King Sivi showed, a gift given whole, what he would most want to keep, asked for nothing back. Today's word.
Your line: what he gave. He gave it gladly, and asked nothing back. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Sivi story is told in Buddhist teaching as an example of the perfection of giving (dana); everyday generosity takes smaller forms, like food offered to monastics, gifts to people in need, or time given freely.
